newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks power higher on yen's sharp decline.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks power higher on yen's sharp decline.

text.p: Tokyo stocks powered higher on Thursday, helped by the yen's tumble against the dollar after remarks by an influential Finance Ministry official on currencies and interest rates, brokers said.

The yen's decline sparked hefty buying in Japan's leading exporters, as it eased worries about their profitability. Active buying-back of shares in the banking sector also accelerated a rise in the key stock index, they said.
The 225-share Nikkei average gained 274.53 points, or 1.35 percent, to close at 20,564.46. It rose as high as 20,696.87. Its June futures jumped 270 points to 20,580.
